analysis.title: Global Asset Allocation Insights, November 2026
key_insights: Fidelity Multi Asset has moved to a more balanced risk stance. Credit is upgraded to neutral, joining equities, government bonds and cash at neutral. Growth is moderating from elevated levels, and persistent inflation, higher bond yields and geopolitical uncertainty make the backdrop more stagflationary.
Equities are neutral overall, with a stated bias to add risk on weakness. Strong earnings and the AI investment cycle are offset by slowing growth, higher yields and geopolitical risk.

Japan is the preferred developed equity market on wage-led reflation, resilient earnings and corporate reforms. The EM overweight is kept, but Fidelity closed its Korea and Taiwan trades to cut AI-sensitive exposure as financing risks and volatility rise.

US equities: resilient earnings and improved valuations are offset by higher real yields and growing concerns over AI financing. Europe is pressured by higher energy costs, weaker earnings and tighter ECB policy. UK valuations and defensiveness are outweighed by weak earnings momentum and fiscal uncertainty. Asia Pacific ex Japan is held back by weak Australian earnings, persistent inflation and a hawkish RBA.

Credit upgraded to neutral after modest spread widening improved risk-reward. High yield is raised to overweight on attractive all-in yields and resilient fundamentals, with limited reliance on further spread compression. Investment grade stays the least preferred area because spreads are tight and AI-linked issuance is a technical headwind. EM hard-currency debt is neutral.

Government bonds are neutral on duration. Higher nominal and real yields improve valuations, but persistent inflation, fiscal pressure and heavy issuance limit a broad rally. Equity-bond correlation is positive, though it has recently decreased. A sustained fall in inflation or a meaningful growth slowdown would improve the outlook.

Fidelity prefers UK Gilts, arguing markets price a more hawkish Bank of England than is likely. It is underweight Bunds (ECB tightening, French fiscal uncertainty) and JGBs (policy normalisation, fiscal risk). US Treasuries are held neutral, citing resilient US growth, further Fed tightening and fiscal concerns.

Currencies: overweight the US dollar on resilient growth, a more hawkish Fed, favourable rate differentials, geopolitics and elevated oil prices. Underweight the euro (French fiscal uncertainty, energy-related growth risks) and sterling (fiscal concerns, a relatively less hawkish BoE). The yen moves to neutral.

Gold and broad commodities stay positive. Geopolitical and fiscal uncertainty and central-bank demand support gold, though higher yields have reduced conviction. Tight supply and the risk of energy disruption support the commodities overweight.

Best ideas: high yield and quality income equities for income. Japanese and EM equities, plus electrification, grid infrastructure and energy security, for growth. Gold and options strategies for downside protection. Absolute return strategies for uncorrelated returns.

Other tactical views: Japan mid-caps and banks (domestic reflation, monetary normalisation), European defence (multi-year budget tailwind, valuations require selectivity), and US transportation with a preference for rail (tightening supply is lifting pricing before demand recovers, positioning is clean).

Watch list: the Iran conflict and energy-driven inflation, a shift in AI focus from capex commitments to cash generation, profitability and funding sustainability, and whether slowing leading indicators turn into weaker activity and how central banks respond.

sector_views.rationale: Banks benefit from monetary policy normalisation and a more favourable interest rate environment.
Mid-caps give exposure to domestic growth and corporate reform beyond large-cap exporters.
Rising procurement budgets and domestic supply-chain efforts give a multi-year tailwind, though valuations and near-term sentiment require selectivity.
Tightening supply is improving pricing before demand has recovered. Rail has the best balance of volumes and pricing, and positioning is relatively clean after recent weakness.
Resilient cash flows and relative defensiveness if inflation risks persist.

sector_views.sector: Electrification, grid infrastructure and energy security
sector_views.rationale: Longer-term investment demand supports them, with growing focus on earnings visibility and financing resilience.

earnings_insights: Fidelity describes corporate earnings as continuing to grow strongly, supported by an AI investment cycle that increasingly benefits the wider economy. The report gives no specific EPS or revenue figures.
Earnings revisions chart (equally weighted 1, 3 and 6M) is titled 'Earnings resilience broadens beyond AI'. The text gives no revision levels.
Regional earnings views: Japan resilient, EM strong, US resilient, Europe weaker, UK weak momentum, Australia weak.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fidelity cites further Fed tightening as a balancing factor for US Treasuries and describes a more hawkish Fed as supportive of the dollar.
ECB tightening is a threat to the European equity recovery and weighs on Bunds.

macro_indicators.reading: Markets price a more hawkish BoE than is likely to materialise
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the Gilt overweight and limits sterling upside.
Limits upside for Asia Pacific ex Japan equities.
Supports the dollar near term. Government bond yields have been driven by oil this year, per the chart title.
Combined with persistent inflation and higher yields, this makes the environment more stagflationary.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight high yield credit for carry
trade_ideas.rationale: Attractive all-in yields and resilient fundamentals, with limited reliance on further spread compression.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Japanese equities, including mid-caps and banks
trade_ideas.rationale: Wage-led reflation, resilient earnings, corporate reforms and monetary normalisation.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight emerging market equities while closing Korea and Taiwan trades
trade_ideas.rationale: Attractive valuations and strong earnings, with reduced AI beta because of financing risks.
trade_ideas.risk: AI capex sustainability and financing risks.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight UK Gilts, underweight Bunds and JGBs
trade_ideas.rationale: Gilts offer attractive relative value and markets price a more hawkish BoE than likely.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US dollar, underweight euro and sterling
trade_ideas.rationale: Resilient US growth, rate differentials and geopolitical uncertainty favour the dollar. French fiscal uncertainty and energy-related growth risks weigh on the euro, and fiscal concerns weigh on sterling.

trade_ideas.description: Hold gold and overweight broad commodities
trade_ideas.rationale: Central-bank demand, geopolitical and fiscal uncertainty, tight supply and energy disruption risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher yields have moderated conviction on gold.

trade_ideas.description: Options strategies for targeted downside protection
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong fundamentals are balanced by elevated risks, and traditional diversification is less reliable.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US rail within US transportation
trade_ideas.rationale: Improving volumes and pricing as the freight cycle turns, with clean positioning.

risk_factors: Iran conflict escalation or energy supply disruption renewing inflation.
Persistent inflation and higher bond yields creating a prolonged stagflationary environment.
AI financing pressures, free cash flow and funding sustainability, including elevated AI-linked debt issuance.
Slowing leading indicators turning into weaker activity.
Fiscal pressures and heavy government bond issuance, including French fiscal uncertainty.
Dollar strength and divergent fundamentals for EM FX and EM local debt.
vol_and_positioning: Fidelity says options strategies can provide targeted downside protection while keeping upside exposure, and finds them particularly useful now because fundamentals are strong but risks are elevated and traditional diversification is less reliable. No strikes, expiries or instruments are given.
Positive equity-bond correlation makes duration additive to portfolio risk, though the correlation has decreased recently.
US transportation positioning is described as relatively clean after recent weakness.
Fidelity says it would look to add risk on weakness.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: further escalation or disruption to energy supplies could renew inflation pressures and prolong a stagflationary environment.
French fiscal uncertainty weighs on the euro and on euro government bonds through sovereign spread volatility.
Geopolitical fragmentation is accelerating European defence spending needs.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong corporate earnings and the AI investment cycle continue to underpin growth, and earnings resilience is broadening beyond AI.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing pressures and questions about free cash flow and the sustainability of AI capex are becoming more important, and AI-linked debt issuance is a headwind for investment grade credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fidelity says the focus is shifting from capex commitments to cash generation, profitability and funding sustainability. No specific level or event is named.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher nominal and real yields have improved valuations, particularly if growth continues to moderate.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent inflation, fiscal pressures and heavy issuance limit a broad rally, and positive equity-bond correlation reduces diversification value.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more sustained decline in inflation or a meaningful growth slowdown would improve the outlook for government bonds.
